headline: Celtics stomp Philly on the road as Toronto looms tonight
morning_brew: What a hell of a night in Philadelphia. The C's walked into the Xfinity Mobile Arena and absolutely took it to the 76ers in a 123-101 win that had me grinning like an idiot all through the second half. It was the kind of performance that makes you feel like a genius for sitting through the early-season noise instead of tossing the remote out the window. Paul George was on another planet, hitting six shots from deep and finishing with thirty-six points, while the bench stepped up and provided the kind of energy that puts teams away early. I haven't seen Philly look that lost since my neighbor Rick tried to assemble a bookshelf without reading the instructions.

Payton Pritchard was the spark plug we needed, pouring in eighteen points and dishing out five assists with a plus-minus that made my jaw drop. The ball movement was surgical, and when you see guys like Sam Hauser knocking down four triples in eighteen minutes, you know the rhythm is back. Defensively, we were flying around, forcing Philly into bad looks and cleaning up the glass. This is the team basketball we expect from a group fighting for the top of the East, and it was a massive relief to see them handle business against a rival without needing a cardiac finish for once.

We have no time to celebrate, though, because we are back at it tonight in Toronto. The Scotiabank Arena is never an easy place to play, and our boys are gonna have to bring that same road intensity to keep the momentum going. I'll be glued to the screen again, hoping for a repeat of that defensive clinic. It is a quick turnaround, but that is the life of a contender in this league, and I for one am ready to see if we can make it two wins in two nights and add a decent deposit to the Duck Boat fund.

trend_watch.trend: Paul George torched the 76ers for thirty-six points on fourteen-of-twenty-two shooting including six-of-eleven from beyond the arc.
trend_watch.dans_take: He was absolutely unconscious, playing like he was in his own backyard hoop session.

trend_watch.trend: Payton Pritchard provided a massive boost off the bench with eighteen points and five assists while shooting four-of-eight from three-point range.
trend_watch.dans_take: Pritchard brings an energy that shifts the whole floor and keeps the defense guessing.

trend_watch.trend: Sam Hauser was perfect from deep in his limited run, hitting four of his six attempts from beyond the arc to finish with twelve points.
trend_watch.dans_take: You leave him open, you pay the price, simple as that, he is automatic.

news_digest.headline: Boston takes road win streak into matchup with Toronto
news_digest.dans_take: We need to stay sharp after that Philly demolition if we want to keep this train rolling.
